en.question: An agent performs a long chain of tool calls where most steps are simple lookups and one step is a difficult synthesis. What is the most cost-effective architecture?

options.text: Run the entire chain on the most capable model for behavioural consistency.
options.note: Paying premium rates for trivial lookups is the commonest avoidable agent cost.

options.text: Run routine steps on a cheap fast model and the synthesis on the capable one.
Run the whole chain on the cheapest tier and accept weaker synthesis quality.
options.note: Degrading the one step that matters defeats the purpose of the chain.

options.text: Run the chain on two different models and compare the results at the end.
options.note: Doubles spend with no reliable way to arbitrate between the two results.

en.explanation: Model choice is a per-step decision rather than a per-application one. Cheap models handle lookups and routing; the expensive model is reserved for the step whose quality decides the outcome.
